steps.prompt: The knight moves in an L: two squares in one direction and one square sideways. It is the only piece that can jump over others.
steps.explanation: The knight moves in an L: two squares in one direction and one square sideways. It is the only piece that can jump over others.

steps.prompt: Tap any square the knight on d4 can jump to.
steps.explanation: A knight in the centre has eight possible squares, all of the opposite colour to the one it stands on.
steps.hint: Two steps then one step to the side.

steps.prompt: Capture the black pawn on e6.
steps.explanation: The pawn is two squares up and one to the right of the knight: an L-shape.

steps.prompt: Which piece can jump over other pieces?
steps.explanation: Only knights jump. That is why they are strong in cramped positions.
steps.hint: It is the piece shaped like a horse.

steps.prompt: Jump a knight out toward the centre.
steps.explanation: Knights are best developed toward the centre, to f3 or c3 for White.
steps.hint: Knights on the rim are dim: aim for f3 or c3.
